why: The added guidance to treat multiword names/dates/measures as atomic (and the new numeric/date example) made the scorer avoid cuts inside those spans, improving H_set on longer pieces. However, the shortened paraphrase of C8 together with the new complement-check wording caused scorers to overprotect those spans and shift cuts earlier (splitting verbs/heads and producing many tiny pieces), harming the short-piece bins (≤3 and ≤5).
lesson: Keep the explicit caution about punctuation/commas and balance atomic-unit protection so it doesn't push cuts onto verb heads or create many tiny fragments (which mainly hurts the ≤3 and ≤5 bins).
